title: Fleet readiness status in internal ops console (table views, filters, drill-down)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
## Goal
Expose the new provision-to-ready readiness state (Allocated / Provisioning / Validating / Ready / Quarantined) and actionable failure context in the internal ops console.

This is internal-only UX for Fleet + SRE + Platform to:
- spot stuck bring-ups quickly (especially “Validating”)
- understand the failure reason/step without jumping across multiple tools
- drill into per-node validation artifacts (timestamps, step timings, log pointers)

## Non-goals
- No customer-facing UI.
- No major workflow changes (e.g., scheduler, pool orchestration). Phase 1 is primarily visibility; operator actions can follow if API support is ready.

## Target users
- Infra/Fleet on-call (triaging new capacity or Dedicated expansions)
- SRE (tracking SLOs, failure modes, alert follow-up)
- Platform (control-plane readiness integration debugging)

## Primary surfaces
### 1) Fleet Readiness Overview (pool-centric)
A page (or console section) that answers: “Is capacity bring-up healthy right now?”

**Top summary cards**
- Nodes by state: Allocated / Provisioning / Validating / Ready / Quarantined
- Top failure reasons (last 24h) + count
- Time-to-ready P50/P95 (last 24h) (if available in API; otherwise link to Grafana)

**Primary table: Pools** (default view)
Columns:
- Pool name / Pool ID
- Deployment mode (Dedicated / Shared)
- Region
- GPU type (A100/H100/etc.)
- Image channel (candidate/stable) + image version (truncated)
- Ready % (Ready / Total)
- In progress (Allocated+Provisioning+Validating)
- Quarantined count
- Latest failure reason (most common or most recent, see data contract notes)
- Updated (last transition time)

Filters:
- Region
- GPU type
- Pool type (Dedicated/Shared)
- Readiness state (multi-select)
- Image channel
- Updated within (15m/1h/24h/custom)
- Text search: pool id/name

Sort:
- Quarantined desc
- Ready % asc
- Updated desc

**Interaction**
- Clicking a pool opens Pool Detail.

### 2) Pool Detail (node-centric)
A detail page scoped to a single pool.

**Header**
- Pool ID/name, region, GPU type, image channel+version
- Current rollout flag status (if available)
- Quick links: Terraform module output (if available), Grafana dashboard, runbook

**Node table**
Columns:
- Node identifier (hostname or internal node ID; confirm canonical field)
- Current readiness state
- Current step (if in Provisioning/Validating) e.g., “kubelet join”, “nccl-smoke-test”
- Failure reason (short)
- Failure category (GPU health / Driver parity / Network / Storage / K8s join / Perf canary / Unknown)
- Attempts (current step attempts)
- Duration in current state
- Last updated

Filters:
- State
- Failure category
- Step name
- Image version (if pool supports mixed during rollout)
- “Stuck > X minutes” toggle

Row click -> Node Detail.

### 3) Node Detail (drill-down)
A drill-down panel/page that answers: “What failed, where do I look, what do I do next?”

**Sections**
- Current status: state + last transition time
- Timeline: Allocated -> Provisioning -> Validating -> Ready/Quarantined with timestamps
- Validation steps list (most recent run):
  - step name
  - start/end
  - duration
  - result (pass/fail/skip)
  - log/artifact pointer (link out)
  - failure summary (short)
- Suggested next actions (copy-first, buttons later):
  - Retry validation (if supported)
  - Drain + reimage (link to runbook steps)
  - Quarantine (if supported)

**Empty states + fallbacks**
- If log pointers aren’t present: show “Artifacts not available” with last known error message.
- If node is missing heartbeat: show “No agent heartbeat” banner + recommended checks.

## Information architecture / navigation
Proposal: Add a top-level left-nav item under Infra/Ops: **Fleet Readiness**.
- Default: Overview (Pools)
- Pool detail and Node detail as subroutes.

## Data contract assumptions (needs confirmation)
From Platform: Fleet Readiness Service will provide:
- Pool readiness summary counts by state
- Node readiness records:
  - state
  - last_transition_at
  - current_step_name (nullable)
  - failure_reason_short (nullable)
  - failure_category (nullable)
  - validation_run_id / latest_validation_at (nullable)
- Validation artifacts:
  - step results array (step name, status, duration, log pointer)

If the service cannot provide ‘top failure reasons’ aggregated, we can compute client-side from nodes within the selected pool scope (but avoid heavy queries across all nodes globally).

## Permissions / access
Internal console already gated; confirm whether Fleet Readiness endpoints are restricted (read-only for most; mutation actions limited).
UI should:
- hide action buttons by default
- render a ‘Read-only’ badge if user lacks mutate permissions

## Acceptance criteria
- Operators can view readiness state for pools and drill down to node details.
- Operators can filter to quickly find Quarantined nodes or nodes stuck in Validating.
- Failure reason and step are visible without leaving the console (even if artifacts link out).
- Works at realistic fleet sizes (avoid rendering thousands of nodes without pagination).

## Open questions
1) Canonical ‘node id’ for UI: k8s node name vs cloud instance id vs internal node UUID?
2) Which failure reason should appear on pool row: most recent failure across nodes vs most common failure category?
3) Pagination + performance constraints: max nodes returned per pool; default to 50/100 rows.
4) Should we display image version at node-level (if mixed versions are possible during rollout)?

## References
- ADR: Provision-to-ready readiness state machine (Allocated/Provisioning/Validating/Ready/Quarantined)
- Runbook: provision-to-ready failures triage
- API proto notes: Fleet readiness endpoints + sample payloads

## Deliverables
- IA + wireframes for Overview, Pool Detail, Node Detail
- Column/filter definitions (final)
- States + failure category mapping spec (display strings)
- Empty/error states

## Notes
This ticket is designed to unblock staged rollout operations. It’s okay to ship Phase 1 as ‘read-only visibility’ with external links to logs/runbooks; action buttons can be a follow-up once APIs stabilize.
